newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Zastava Cars says no decision on JV yet.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Zastava Cars says no decision on JV yet.

text.p: Yugoslav carmaker Zastava has still not chosen its joint venture partner among three foreign companies it has been negotiating with, Zastava Group President Srboljub Vasovic said on Thursday.
"Intensive talks have been reduced to three partners -- one from the far east and two from Europe," Vasovic told a news conference on the eve of the Belgrade International Car Show.
His comments poured cold water on repeated reports that South Korea's Hyundai Motor Company was on the verge of clinching a deal.
Vasovic only said "intensive negotiations" were in progress with Hyundai but added he was not at liberty to reveal the names of the other two companies yet, although he did let slip Italy's Fiat.
According to Vasovic, negotiations with Renault of France have been "frozen".

"Perhaps the negotiations have been slow, but they could be even slower since our country at this moment is not too interesting from the aspect of stability, either economic or political," Vasovic said.

Zastava Cars is looking for foreign investors to provide capital to revitalise production which last year barely reached 10,000 cars from nearly 200,000 in 1990, before the breakup of former Yugoslavia. Zastava plans to produce 150,000 cars by the year 2001 if it finds a joint venture partner.
Despite a modest start, Zastava is sticking by earlier announced plans to produce 30,000 vehicles this year, half of which will be exported.

"The exports of 15,000 cars are much more certain since deals have already been concluded. It will be much harder to sell the other 15,000 on the local market in view of the population's deteriorating purchasing power," Vasovic said.
Economic recession, along with declining wages and standard of living, do not offer a promising outlook for car sales on the Yugoslav market.

Zastava's main difficulties at the start of the year remain lack of working capital, engines and other parts produced by local manufacturers who have similar problems. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
